claim: 1. Frontier training costs hundreds of millions to >$1bn; returns incremental not exponential
evidence: GPT-4 $78m compute; Gemini Ultra ~$192m; Llama 3.1 405B ~$170m (Stanford AI Index 2025). >$1bn single run is projected for ~2027 (Epoch AI/Cottier et al. 2025), not yet documented. Cost per fixed capability fell >280x in ~18 months (GPT-3.5 level $20.00 to $0.07 per million tokens).
source: Stanford AI Index 2025; Epoch AI arXiv:2405.21015

evidence: $300bn is OpenAI's purchase obligation TO Oracle (~5 years from 2027, 4.5 GW), not Oracle's own spend. Oracle RPO $455bn at 31 Aug 2025 (+359% YoY). Total debt ~$105-112bn. Moody's Baa2 / S&P BBB negative outlook.
source: WSJ Sep 2025; Oracle 8-K 30 Jun 2025; Oracle Q1 FY2026

claim: 3. Circular financing NVIDIA / hyperscalers / OpenAI / Anthropic
evidence: IMF GFSR Oct 13 2026: 14 deals since 2023, $300bn equity + $650bn debt for $1.4tn future revenue commitments. BIS Bulletin 137: 55.2% of AI investment from other AI firms; 46.4% of AI-to-AI deal value had an investor who was also a supplier or customer. No regulator found fraudulent round-tripping.
source: IMF GFSR Oct 2026; BIS Bulletin No.137 Oct 1 2026

evidence: Four hyperscalers $416bn capex 2025 (+66%); 2026 guidance ~$645bn+. Financed mostly from operating cash flow plus rapidly rising debt. No hyperscaler discloses data-centre or GPU utilisation.

claim: 5. End of free AI and thin wrappers
evidence: Per-token prices fell sharply; total bills and subscription tiers tightened. Thin wrappers failing in large numbers (Jasper revenue -54%; Builder.ai bankruptcy May 2025) while workflow-deep products thrive (Cursor ~$2bn ARR; Claude Code $2.5bn run-rate). AI hiring strong for senior roles, weaker for entry-level.
